findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed that a sanitizing solution was not available when Inspector arrived despite food preparation having just started. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and made a sanitizing bucket that tested at 100ppm (Chlorine), a safe and effective concentration of that sanitizer (Chlorine should be between 50-200ppm). Inspector discussed with the PIC that a sanitizing solution should be available at all times during food preparation for sanitizing surfaces, not just during times of warewashing. Ensure that a sanitizing solution is available for use for all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

The wood in this area must be repaired/replaced with a material that is smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that these surfaces meet this criteria by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed three half-gallon containers of 2% milk in the silver uprights in the back storage area. All three containers of milk were open and none bore a date mark. Two of the containers had not reached the manufacturers expiration date but one had expired as of 10/15/2022. All three containers of milk were at 37 degrees F; below the 41 degree F requirement for temperature. The container of milk which had expired was discarded and person-in-charge believes the milk may have been previously frozen but was unsure. Person-in-charge will discuss with cook the need to date mark milk containers and ensure that they are date/time marked appropriately. A follow-up will be issued for 10-days at which time inspector will check for proper date marking throughout the facility. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wiping cloths were observed sitting in a shallow container with a small amount of water at the bottom of it. Inspector checked chlorine concentration of the water with tests strips and there was no chlorine present. The wiping cloths appeared to have been left out over night. The wiping cloths were not submerged in water with most of the cloth exposed to the air. Wiping cloths must be stored in chemical sanitizer (bleach water solution) at proper concentrations when not directly in use for wiping surfaces. Wet wiping cloths exposed to the air and stored in water facilitate bacterial growth and pose a contamination hazard. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored submerged in sanitizer solution and are not stored overnight when bleach concentrations of the water cannot be checked as bleach concentrations degrade over time. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Cook was observed washing dishes upon arrival of inspector. A plastic bowl was washed and rinsed prior to being dunked in bleach solution and set aside to air dry. Employee was advised the contact time for the sanitizing step during manual ware washing should be at least 60 seconds. Make sure all items are submerged in sanitizer for at least 1 minute prior to being removed to air dry. Items were re-sanitized.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Contact time for sanitizing step must be 60 seconds.

findings.citation_text:
750.600 - Ziplock bag was re-used for storage of cheese slices in the 2 door cooler. Cook was advised to cease the practice. Ziplock bags are a single use article and must be discarded after use.
 
Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items (e.g. aluminum foil, ziplock bags, plastic wrap, etc.)
